A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BootTrans and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F. Retained, added, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, pivot-language comparisons, and appendix error and test-suite sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds OORL comparisons, extended-language evaluations, and ClassEval-T results.

M1.justification: Sections 2-3, Algorithm 1, and Equations 1-4 retain the same dual-pool procedure, execution reward, language-aware weighting, and GRPO objective. The added evaluations do not introduce a changed BootTrans procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the original Python/Java/C++ coverage, v2 evaluates Go-related directions including JavaScript, low-resource Dlang and Racket targets, and whole-class translation on ClassEval-T. Appendix B also introduces SLTrans C-to-IR data for OORL training.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds OORL as an evaluated Qwen3-1.7B comparison method alongside EffiReasonTrans, CoTran, MultiPL-T, and PPOCoder. The existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Settings for retained experiments, including dataset sizes, training hyperparameters, and greedy decoding, remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce class-level and method-level computational accuracy on ClassEval-T and an OORL setup using 9,600 sampled SLTrans groups for offline training.

E4.justification: New Sections 4.6-4.7 substantially extend generalization analysis by testing languages unseen during BootTrans training, low-resource targets, and transfer to whole classes without class-level training. Existing ablations, pivot comparisons, case examples, error analysis, and test-suite sensitivity results are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds OORL scores and substantial new language-transfer and class-level results in Tables 5-6. For example, new Table 5 reports Python-to-Dlang CA@1 of 23.08 for base Qwen3-1.7B versus 41.67 for BootTrans. Previously reported scores, including the sensitivity results in v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 7, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal problem, pivot-language assumptions, reward definition, weighting formula, and optimization equations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about bootstrapping multilingual data, balancing optimization, and improving benchmark performance. The added evaluations do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 narrows superiority over finetuning baselines from all tasks to benchmark averages, consistent with MultiPL-T's 86.08 versus BootTrans's 85.87 on TransCoder-Test Python-to-C++. New discussion interprets language transfer and attributes weak class-level Java-to-C++ performance to model capacity and C++ complexity. The case study also drops its computational-efficiency assertion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and documents OORL's online/offline data setup, including the 9,600 SLTrans groups in Appendix B. Section 4.6 specifies MultiPL-E test conversion for the low-resource evaluations. Existing BootTrans implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Wu et al. for OORL, Oida-Onesa and Ballera for low-resource languages, and Xue et al. for ClassEval-T. OORL enters the related-work discussion, while the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized prose and acronym edits, two new experimental subsections, case-study renumbering, and added acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two result tables and an OORL row in Table 2, and corrects Table 2's best-score bolding for TransCoder-Test Python-to-C++. Existing figures are retained with layout shifts; the appendix sensitivity table is renumbered from Table 5 to Table 7.

improvement.justification: The added transfer tests and OORL comparison strengthen empirical support and reveal applicability limits beyond v1's evaluation. Code-access information and corrected Table 2 wording and highlighting also improve the paper. The gain is limited by briefly specified new evaluations and the retained blanket same-dataset claim despite OORL's additional offline SLTrans data.
